description: Team Zenith is building Martian Map 2026, an interactive mapping and navigation platform focused on Mars and the Curiosity rover’s landing region. We’re a motivated team with experience in data, visualization and web development, and we care about making space exploration safer and easier to understand. We’re looking for a UI/UX designer and someone with a passion for planetary science. If you love space, join us.
summary:
Martian Map 2026 is an interactive mapping and navigation platform for Gale Crater, where NASA’s Curiosity rover landed in 2012. It combines 3D terrain with hazard analysis to plan safer routes on Mars.

Problem. Rovers drive on pre-planned routes because of communication delay, yet traction, lighting, dust, temperature, and pressure are rarely combined in one view, and they change over time.

Solution. One terrain model carries six hazard layers: sunlight, atmosphere, electrostatic discharge, surface friction, red danger zones, and the water triple point. Time-based shadow simulation and horizon analysis support observation planning. Users drop pins, and the platform calculates a route that avoids danger zones and low-traction slopes, with step-by-step elevation guidance.

Validation. Routes are compared with Curiosity’s historical path, and modeled conditions with REMS pressure and temperature records.

Impact. Planners, scientists, and students can compare routes on evidence, using only public NASA data.

Limits. Orbital data cannot resolve wheel-scale rocks, and friction and electrostatic layers are estimates, shown with uncertainty.
details:
- Interactive 3D Mars exploration simulator

- Renders a detailed Mars terrain surface in a browser using a 3D map generated from a high-resolution digital terrain model.

- Includes a first-person astronaut view and an overhead map view.

- You can look around by moving the mouse and rotate the camera freely.

- Multiple terrain visualization modes

- Terrain lit by sunlight

- Slope hazard map

- Hillshade relief view

- Grip margin / traction map

- These modes can be switched in real time from the control panel.

- Adjustable terrain assumptions

- Lets the user change the assumed soil friction value (μ) using a slider.

- Updates slip thresholds and traction risk instantly.

- This is used to simulate how slope steepness affects mobility.

- Dynamic local time simulation

- Local time can be adjusted through the day cycle.

- Lighting and scene color respond to the selected time of day.

- Sun angle and Mars atmosphere are updated live.

- Safety and hazard simulation

- Terrain is classified by slope danger:

- safe flat ground

- moderate slope

- steep slope

- cliff / no-go terrain

- Walking is blocked on ground steeper than roughly 20°.

- Slipping behavior is modeled using traction demand vs. friction.

- Low traction warnings trigger before dangerous conditions.

- Mission status HUD

- Displays:

- heading

- elevation

- ground type

- friction coefficient

- slip threshold

- traction use

- grip status

- EVA time

- suit temperature

- oxygen remaining

- dose so far

- distance to base

- return margin

- Suit and environmental realism

- Simulates Mars gravity and jumping behavior.

- Includes thermal changes based on terrain, sunlight, and movement.

- Tracks suit temperature and warns if conditions become too hot.

- Includes oxygen reserve and emergency return logic.

- Route planning

- Uses a grid-based A* pathfinding system to compute safe walking routes.

- Can plan a route to:

- the next science stop

- a selected map pin

- the base

- Shows estimated distance and travel time.

- Supports route follow automation.

- Science stop system

- Multiple science stop markers are placed on safe terrain.

- Completing a stop marks it as reached and updates mission progress.

- A photo panel appears when a stop is reached.

- The route system can optimize a safe tour across all remaining stops.

- Full map explorer

- Opens a large map window with pan, zoom, and search functions.

- Can search by:

- base

- stop number

- coordinate values

- Allows clicking a location to create a pin and plan a path there.

- Can switch between a photo layer, slope layer, and grip layer in the map.

- Historical Gale Crater overview

- Includes a separate Gale Crater map view with historical Curiosity route data.

- Shows approximate mission landmarks and their development across the mission timeline.

- Lets the user browse a terrain gallery with multiple DTM / image layers.

- Includes a local overview of the mapped area and historical traverse.

- Visual effects and atmosphere

- Adds dust particles, drifting motes, and footsteps / landing puffs.

- Creates a more realistic Mars environment with moving dust under simulated gravity and wind.

- Uses a stylized sky and camera effects to reinforce the Mars setting.

- Solar particle event toggle

- User can simulate a solar particle event.

- This increases radiation dose dramatically and gives a mission warning.

- Useful for exploring crew safety tradeoffs and return timing.

- Live position sharing

- Same-browser live sharing is supported for simulated positions.

- Allows multiple tabs to see each other’s simulated location.

- Useful for collaborative walkthroughs or demo sessions.

- Controls and user interaction

- Keyboard movement:

- W/A/S/D to move

- Shift to move faster

- V to switch view

- M to open/close the map

- R to plan route

- F to follow route

- B to abort and return to base

- Mouse wheel zooming and map dragging.

- Pointer lock for immersive first-person walking.

- Mission planning and performance monitoring

- Tracks how much time has been spent on EVA and whether a safe return still exists.

- Gives a “return margin” warning when time is running low.

- Helps users think through astronaut surface operations and mission risk.

- Map-based waypoint context

- Base and science stops are shown visually on the map.

- A travel trail is kept to show past movement and route history.

- Helps the user understand traversed distance and path planning.

- Clean user interface

- Uses a compact mission console style with interactive controls and status panels.

- Overlay panels show mission information without cluttering the main terrain view.

- Multi-layer data integration

- Combines:

- terrain height data

- slope hazard image

- hillshade texture

- orthographic image

- waypoint metadata

- mission planning grid

- All are blended into one immersive exploration experience.
